457: ///
458: /// This type is generic over `W`, which represents any implementation
459: /// of the `termcolor::WriteColor` trait. If colors are not desired,
460: /// then the `new_no_color` constructor can be used, or, alternatively,
461: /// the `termcolor::NoColor` adapter can be used to wrap any `io::Write`
462: /// implementation without enabling any colors.

464: pub struct Standard<W> {
465:     config: Config,
466:     wtr: RefCell<CounterWriter<W>>,
467:     matches: Vec<Match>,
468: }

472:     /// matches to the given writer.
473:     ///
474:     /// The writer should be an implementation of `termcolor::WriteColor`
475:     /// and not just a bare implementation of `io::Write`. To use a normal
476:     /// `io::Write` implementation (simultaneously sacrificing colors), use
477:     /// the `new_no_color` constructor.
478:     pub fn new(wtr: W) -> Standard<W> {
479:         StandardBuilder::new().build(wtr)

481: }

485:     /// matches to the given writer.

488:     /// constructor, the printer will never emit colors.
489:     pub fn new_no_color(wtr: W) -> Standard<NoColor<W>> {

491:     }

494: impl<W: WriteColor> Standard<W> {
495:     /// Return an implementation of `Sink` for the standard printer.
496:     ///
497:     /// This does not associate the printer with a file path, which means this
498:     /// implementation will never print a file path along with the matches.
499:     pub fn sink<'s, M: Matcher>(
500:         &'s mut self,
501:         matcher: M,
502:     ) -> StandardSink<'static, 's, M, W> {
503:         let stats = if self.config.stats { Some(Stats::new()) } else { None };
504:         let mut replacer = Replacer::new();
505:         replacer.install_color_specs(&self.config.colors);
506:         let supports_color = self.wtr.borrow().supports_color();
507:         let needs_match_granularity = replacer.needs_match_granularity(
508:             supports_color,
509:             !self.config.colors.matched().is_none(),
510:             self.config.column,
511:             self.config.replacement.is_some(),
512:             self.config.per_match,
513:             self.config.only_matching,
514:             self.config.stats,
515:         );
516:         StandardSink {
517:             matcher: matcher,
518:             standard: self,
519:             replacer: replacer,
520:             path: None,
521:             start_time: Instant::now(),
522:             match_count: 0,
523:             after_context_remaining: 0,
524:             binary_byte_offset: None,
525:             stats: stats,
526:             needs_match_granularity: needs_match_granularity,
527:         }
528:     }

530:     /// Return an implementation of `Sink` associated with a file path.
531:     ///
532:     /// When the printer is associated with a path, then it may, depending on
533:     /// its configuration, print the path along with the matches found.
534:     pub fn sink_with_path<'p, 's, M, P>(
535:         &'s mut self,
536:         matcher: M,
537:         path: &'p P,
538:     ) -> StandardSink<'p, 's, M, W>

540:         M: Matcher,
541:         P: ?Sized + AsRef<Path>,
542:     {

544:             return self.sink(matcher);

548:             path.as_ref(),
549:             self.config.separator_path,
550:         );
551:         let mut replacer = Replacer::new();
552:         replacer.install_color_specs(&self.config.colors);
553:         let supports_color = self.wtr.borrow().supports_color();
554:         let needs_match_granularity = replacer.needs_match_granularity(
555:             supports_color,
556:             !self.config.colors.matched().is_none(),
557:             self.config.column,
558:             self.config.replacement.is_some(),
559:             self.config.per_match,
560:             self.config.only_matching,
561:             self.config.stats,
562:         );
563:         StandardSink {
564:             matcher: matcher,
565:             standard: self,
566:             replacer: replacer,
567:             path: Some(ppath),
568:             start_time: Instant::now(),
569:             match_count: 0,
570:             after_context_remaining: 0,
571:             binary_byte_offset: None,
572:             stats: stats,
573:             needs_match_granularity: needs_match_granularity,
574:         }
575:     }

577:     /// Returns true if and only if the configuration of the printer requires
578:     /// us to find each individual match in the lines reported by the searcher.
579:     ///
580:     /// We care about this distinction because finding each individual match
581:     /// costs more, so we only do it when we need to.
582:     fn needs_match_granularity(&self) -> bool {
583:         let supports_color = self.wtr.borrow().supports_color();
584:         let match_colored = !self.config.colors.matched().is_none();
585: 
586:         // Coloring requires identifying each individual match.
587:         (supports_color && match_colored)
588:         // The column feature requires finding the position of the first match.
589:         || self.config.column
590:         // Requires finding each match for performing replacement.
591:         || self.config.replacement.is_some()
592:         // Emitting a line for each match requires finding each match.
593:         || self.config.per_match
594:         // Emitting only the match requires finding each match.
595:         || self.config.only_matching
596:         // Computing certain statistics requires finding each match.
597:         || self.config.stats
598:     }
599: }

620: /// An implementation of `Sink` associated with a matcher and an optional file
621: /// path for the standard printer.
622: ///
623: /// A `Sink` can be created via the
624: /// [`Standard::sink`](struct.Standard.html#method.sink)
625: /// or
626: /// [`Standard::sink_with_path`](struct.Standard.html#method.sink_with_path)
627: /// methods, depending on whether you want to include a file path in the
628: /// printer's output.
629: ///
630: /// Building a `StandardSink` is cheap, and callers should create a new one
631: /// for each thing that is searched. After a search has completed, callers may
632: /// query this sink for information such as whether a match occurred or whether
633: /// binary data was found (and if so, the offset at which it occurred).
634: ///
635: /// This type is generic over a few type parameters:
636: ///
637: /// * `'p` refers to the lifetime of the file path, if one is provided. When
638: ///   no file path is given, then this is `'static`.
639: /// * `'s` refers to the lifetime of the
640: ///   [`Standard`](struct.Standard.html)
641: ///   printer that this type borrows.
642: /// * `M` refers to the type of matcher used by
643: ///   `grep_searcher::Searcher` that is reporting results to this sink.
644: /// * `W` refers to the underlying writer that this printer is writing its
645: ///   output to.
646: #[derive(Debug)]
647: pub struct StandardSink<'p, 's, M: Matcher, W> {
648:     matcher: M,
649:     standard: &'s mut Standard<W>,
650:     replacer: Replacer<M>,
651:     path: Option<PrinterPath<'p>>,
652:     start_time: Instant,
653:     match_count: u64,
654:     after_context_remaining: u64,
655:     binary_byte_offset: Option<u64>,
656:     stats: Option<Stats>,
657:     needs_match_granularity: bool,
658: }

660: impl<'p, 's, M: Matcher, W: WriteColor> StandardSink<'p, 's, M, W> {
661:     /// Returns true if and only if this printer received a match in the
662:     /// previous search.
663:     ///
664:     /// This is unaffected by the result of searches before the previous
665:     /// search on this sink.
666:     pub fn has_match(&self) -> bool {
667:         self.match_count > 0
668:     }
669: 
670:     /// Return the total number of matches reported to this sink.
671:     ///
672:     /// This corresponds to the number of times `Sink::matched` is called
673:     /// on the previous search.
674:     ///
675:     /// This is unaffected by the result of searches before the previous
676:     /// search on this sink.
677:     pub fn match_count(&self) -> u64 {
678:         self.match_count
679:     }
680: 
681:     /// If binary data was found in the previous search, this returns the
682:     /// offset at which the binary data was first detected.
683:     ///
684:     /// The offset returned is an absolute offset relative to the entire
685:     /// set of bytes searched.
686:     ///
687:     /// This is unaffected by the result of searches before the previous
688:     /// search. e.g., If the search prior to the previous search found binary
689:     /// data but the previous search found no binary data, then this will
690:     /// return `None`.
691:     pub fn binary_byte_offset(&self) -> Option<u64> {
692:         self.binary_byte_offset
693:     }
694: 
695:     /// Return a reference to the stats produced by the printer for all
696:     /// searches executed on this sink.
697:     ///
698:     /// This only returns stats if they were requested via the
699:     /// [`StandardBuilder`](struct.StandardBuilder.html)
700:     /// configuration.
701:     pub fn stats(&self) -> Option<&Stats> {
702:         self.stats.as_ref()
703:     }
704: 
705:     /// Execute the matcher over the given bytes and record the match
706:     /// locations if the current configuration demands match granularity.
707:     fn record_matches(
708:         &mut self,
709:         searcher: &Searcher,
710:         bytes: &[u8],
711:         range: std::ops::Range<usize>,
712:     ) -> io::Result<()> {
713:         self.standard.matches.clear();
714:         if !self.needs_match_granularity {
715:             self.replacer.clear_recorded_matches();
716:             return Ok(());
717:         }
718:         self.replacer.record_matches_in_context(
719:             searcher,
720:             &self.matcher,
721:             bytes,
722:             range.clone(),
723:             |_| true,
724:         )?;
725:         self.standard.matches.extend_from_slice(self.replacer.recorded_matches());
726:         Ok(())
727:     }
728: 
729:     /// If the configuration specifies a replacement, then this executes the
730:     /// replacement, lazily allocating memory if necessary.
731:     ///
732:     /// To access the result of a replacement, use `replacer.replacement()`.
733:     fn replace(
734:         &mut self,
735:         searcher: &Searcher,
736:         bytes: &[u8],
737:         range: std::ops::Range<usize>,
738:     ) -> io::Result<()> {
739:         self.replacer.clear();
740:         if self.standard.config.replacement.is_some() {
741:             let replacement = (*self.standard.config.replacement)
742:                 .as_ref()
743:                 .map(|r| &*r)
744:                 .unwrap();
745:             self.replacer.replace_all(
746:                 searcher,
747:                 &self.matcher,
748:                 bytes,
749:                 range,
750:                 replacement,
751:             )?;
752:         }
753:         Ok(())
754:     }
755: 
756:     /// Returns true if this printer should quit.
757:     ///
758:     /// This implements the logic for handling quitting after seeing a certain
759:     /// amount of matches. In most cases, the logic is simple, but we must
760:     /// permit all "after" contextual lines to print after reaching the limit.
761:     fn should_quit(&self) -> bool {
762:         self.replacer.should_quit_search(
763:             self.match_count,
764:             self.standard.config.max_matches,
765:             self.after_context_remaining,
766:         )
767:     }
768: 
769:     /// Returns whether the current match count exceeds the configured limit.
770:     /// If there is no limit, then this always returns false.
771:     fn match_more_than_limit(&self) -> bool {
772:         self.replacer.match_more_than_limit(
773:             self.match_count,
774:             self.standard.config.max_matches,
775:         )
776:     }
777: }

779: impl<'p, 's, M: Matcher, W: WriteColor> Sink for StandardSink<'p, 's, M, W> {
780:     type Error = io::Error;
781: 
782:     fn matched(
783:         &mut self,
784:         searcher: &Searcher,
785:         mat: &SinkMatch<'_>,
786:     ) -> Result<bool, io::Error> {
787:         self.match_count += 1;
788:         // When we've exceeded our match count, then the remaining context
789:         // lines should not be reset, but instead, decremented. This avoids a
790:         // bug where we display more matches than a configured limit. The main
791:         // idea here is that 'matched' might be called again while printing
792:         // an after-context line. In that case, we should treat this as a
793:         // contextual line rather than a matching line for the purposes of
794:         // termination.
795:         if self.match_more_than_limit() {
796:             self.after_context_remaining = self.replacer.after_context_step(
797:                 true,
798:                 self.after_context_remaining,
799:                 searcher.after_context() as u64,
800:             );
801:         } else {
802:             self.after_context_remaining = self.replacer.after_context_step(
803:                 false,
804:                 self.after_context_remaining,
805:                 searcher.after_context() as u64,
806:             );
807:         }
808: 
809:         self.record_matches(
810:             searcher,
811:             mat.buffer(),
812:             mat.bytes_range_in_buffer(),
813:         )?;
814:         self.replace(searcher, mat.buffer(), mat.bytes_range_in_buffer())?;
815: 
816:         if let Some(ref mut stats) = self.stats {
817:             stats.add_matches(self.standard.matches.len() as u64);
818:             stats.add_matched_lines(mat.lines().count() as u64);
819:         }
820:         if searcher.binary_detection().convert_byte().is_some() {
821:             if self.binary_byte_offset.is_some() {
822:                 return Ok(false);
823:             }
824:         }
825: 
826:         StandardImpl::from_match(searcher, self, mat).sink()?;
827:         Ok(!self.should_quit())
828:     }
829: 
830:     fn context(
831:         &mut self,
832:         searcher: &Searcher,
833:         ctx: &SinkContext<'_>,
834:     ) -> Result<bool, io::Error> {
835:         self.standard.matches.clear();
836:         self.replacer.clear();
837: 
838:         if ctx.kind() == &SinkContextKind::After {
839:             self.after_context_remaining =
840:                 self.after_context_remaining.saturating_sub(1);
841:         }
842:         if searcher.invert_match() {
843:             self.record_matches(searcher, ctx.bytes(), 0..ctx.bytes().len())?;
844:             self.replace(searcher, ctx.bytes(), 0..ctx.bytes().len())?;
845:         }
846:         if searcher.binary_detection().convert_byte().is_some() {
847:             if self.binary_byte_offset.is_some() {
848:                 return Ok(false);
849:             }
850:         }
851: 
852:         StandardImpl::from_context(searcher, self, ctx).sink()?;
853:         Ok(!self.should_quit())
854:     }
855: 
856:     fn context_break(
857:         &mut self,
858:         searcher: &Searcher,
859:     ) -> Result<bool, io::Error> {
860:         StandardImpl::new(searcher, self).write_context_separator()?;
861:         Ok(true)
862:     }
863: 
864:     fn binary_data(
865:         &mut self,
866:         _searcher: &Searcher,
867:         binary_byte_offset: u64,
868:     ) -> Result<bool, io::Error> {
869:         self.binary_byte_offset = Some(binary_byte_offset);
870:         Ok(true)
871:     }
872: 
873:     fn begin(&mut self, _searcher: &Searcher) -> Result<bool, io::Error> {
874:         self.standard.wtr.borrow_mut().reset_count();
875:         self.start_time = Instant::now();
876:         self.match_count = 0;
877:         self.after_context_remaining = 0;
878:         self.binary_byte_offset = None;
879:         if !self.replacer.begin_should_continue(self.standard.config.max_matches)
880:         {
881:             return Ok(false);
882:         }
883:         Ok(true)
884:     }
885: 
886:     fn finish(
887:         &mut self,
888:         searcher: &Searcher,
889:         finish: &SinkFinish,
890:     ) -> Result<(), io::Error> {
891:         if let Some(offset) = self.binary_byte_offset {
892:             StandardImpl::new(searcher, self).write_binary_message(offset)?;
893:         }
894:         if let Some(stats) = self.stats.as_mut() {
895:             stats.add_elapsed(self.start_time.elapsed());
896:             stats.add_searches(1);
897:             if self.match_count > 0 {
898:                 stats.add_searches_with_match(1);
899:             }
900:             stats.add_bytes_searched(finish.byte_count());
901:             stats.add_bytes_printed(self.standard.wtr.borrow().count());
902:         }
903:         Ok(())
904:     }
905: }

907: /// The actual implementation of the standard printer. This couples together
908: /// the searcher, the sink implementation and information about the match.
909: ///
910: /// A StandardImpl is initialized every time a match or a contextual line is
911: /// reported.
912: #[derive(Debug)]
913: struct StandardImpl<'a, M: Matcher, W> {
914:     searcher: &'a Searcher,
915:     sink: &'a StandardSink<'a, 'a, M, W>,
916:     sunk: Sunk<'a>,
917:     /// Set to true if and only if we are writing a match with color.
918:     in_color_match: Cell<bool>,
919: }
920: 
921: impl<'a, M: Matcher, W: WriteColor> StandardImpl<'a, M, W> {
922:     /// Bundle self with a searcher and return the core implementation of Sink.
923:     fn new(
924:         searcher: &'a Searcher,
925:         sink: &'a StandardSink<'_, '_, M, W>,
926:     ) -> StandardImpl<'a, M, W> {
927:         StandardImpl {
928:             searcher: searcher,
929:             sink: sink,
930:             sunk: Sunk::empty(),
931:             in_color_match: Cell::new(false),
932:         }
933:     }
934: 
935:     /// Bundle self with a searcher and return the core implementation of Sink
936:     /// for use with handling matching lines.
937:     fn from_match(
938:         searcher: &'a Searcher,
939:         sink: &'a StandardSink<'_, '_, M, W>,
940:         mat: &'a SinkMatch<'a>,
941:     ) -> StandardImpl<'a, M, W> {
942:         let sunk = Sunk::from_sink_match(
943:             mat,
944:             &sink.standard.matches,
945:             sink.replacer.replacement(),
946:         );
947:         StandardImpl { sunk: sunk, ..StandardImpl::new(searcher, sink) }
948:     }
949: 
950:     /// Bundle self with a searcher and return the core implementation of Sink
951:     /// for use with handling contextual lines.
952:     fn from_context(
953:         searcher: &'a Searcher,
954:         sink: &'a StandardSink<'_, '_, M, W>,
955:         ctx: &'a SinkContext<'a>,
956:     ) -> StandardImpl<'a, M, W> {
957:         let sunk = Sunk::from_sink_context(
958:             ctx,
959:             &sink.standard.matches,
960:             sink.replacer.replacement(),
961:         );
962:         StandardImpl { sunk: sunk, ..StandardImpl::new(searcher, sink) }
963:     }
964: 
965:     fn sink(&self) -> io::Result<()> {
966:         self.write_search_prelude()?;
967:         let strat = self.sink.replacer.sink_strategy(
968:             !self.sunk.matches().is_empty(),
969:             self.multi_line(),
970:             self.is_context(),
971:         );
972:         if strat == 1 {
973:             self.sink_fast_multi_line()
974:         } else if strat == 0 {
975:             self.sink_fast()
976:         } else if strat == 3 {
977:             self.sink_slow_multi_line()
978:         } else {
979:             self.sink_slow()
980:         }
981:     }
982: 
983:     /// Print matches (limited to one line) quickly by avoiding the detection
984:     /// of each individual match in the lines reported in the given
985:     /// `SinkMatch`.
986:     ///
987:     /// This should only be used when the configuration does not demand match
988:     /// granularity and the searcher is not in multi line mode.
989:     fn sink_fast(&self) -> io::Result<()> {
990:         debug_assert!(self.sunk.matches().is_empty());
991:         debug_assert!(!self.multi_line() || self.is_context());
992: 
993:         self.write_prelude(
994:             self.sunk.absolute_byte_offset(),
995:             self.sunk.line_number(),
996:             None,
997:         )?;
998:         self.write_line(self.sunk.bytes())
999:     }
1000: 
1001:     /// Print matches (possibly spanning more than one line) quickly by
1002:     /// avoiding the detection of each individual match in the lines reported
1003:     /// in the given `SinkMatch`.
1004:     ///
1005:     /// This should only be used when the configuration does not demand match
1006:     /// granularity. This may be used when the searcher is in multi line mode.
1007:     fn sink_fast_multi_line(&self) -> io::Result<()> {
1008:         debug_assert!(self.sunk.matches().is_empty());
1009:         let _ = self.sink.replacer.collect_line_ranges(
1010:             self.sunk.bytes(),
1011:             self.searcher.line_terminator().as_byte(),
1012:         );
1013:         // This isn't actually a required invariant for using this method,
1014:         // but if we wind up here and multi line mode is disabled, then we
1015:         // should still treat it as a bug since we should be using matched_fast
1016:         // instead.
1017:         debug_assert!(self.multi_line());
1018: 
1019:         let line_term = self.searcher.line_terminator().as_byte();
1020:         let mut absolute_byte_offset = self.sunk.absolute_byte_offset();
1021:         for (i, line) in self.sunk.lines(line_term).enumerate() {
1022:             self.write_prelude(
1023:                 absolute_byte_offset,
1024:                 self.sunk.line_number().map(|n| n + i as u64),
1025:                 None,
1026:             )?;
1027:             absolute_byte_offset += line.len() as u64;
1028: 
1029:             self.write_line(line)?;
1030:         }
1031:         Ok(())
1032:     }
1033: 
1034:     /// Print a matching line where the configuration of the printer requires
1035:     /// finding each individual match (e.g., for coloring).
1036:     fn sink_slow(&self) -> io::Result<()> {
1037:         debug_assert!(!self.sunk.matches().is_empty());
1038:         debug_assert!(!self.multi_line() || self.is_context());
1039: 
1040:         if self.config().only_matching {
1041:             for &m in self.sunk.matches() {
1042:                 self.write_prelude(
1043:                     self.sunk.absolute_byte_offset() + m.start() as u64,
1044:                     self.sunk.line_number(),
1045:                     Some(m.start() as u64 + 1),
1046:                 )?;
1047: 
1048:                 let buf = &self.sunk.bytes()[m];
1049:                 self.write_colored_line(&[Match::new(0, buf.len())], buf)?;
1050:             }
1051:         } else if self.config().per_match {
1052:             for &m in self.sunk.matches() {
1053:                 self.write_prelude(
1054:                     self.sunk.absolute_byte_offset() + m.start() as u64,
1055:                     self.sunk.line_number(),
1056:                     Some(m.start() as u64 + 1),
1057:                 )?;
1058:                 self.write_colored_line(&[m], self.sunk.bytes())?;
1059:             }
1060:         } else {
1061:             self.write_prelude(
1062:                 self.sunk.absolute_byte_offset(),
1063:                 self.sunk.line_number(),
1064:                 Some(self.sunk.matches()[0].start() as u64 + 1),
1065:             )?;
1066:             self.write_colored_line(self.sunk.matches(), self.sunk.bytes())?;
1067:         }
1068:         Ok(())
1069:     }
1070: 
1071:     fn sink_slow_multi_line(&self) -> io::Result<()> {
1072:         debug_assert!(!self.sunk.matches().is_empty());
1073:         debug_assert!(self.multi_line());
1074: 
1075:         if self.config().only_matching {
1076:             return self.sink_slow_multi_line_only_matching();
1077:         } else if self.config().per_match {
1078:             return self.sink_slow_multi_per_match();
1079:         }
1080: 
1081:         let line_term = self.searcher.line_terminator().as_byte();
1082:         let bytes = self.sunk.bytes();
1083:         let matches = self.sunk.matches();
1084:         let mut midx = 0;
1085:         let mut count = 0;
1086:         let mut stepper = LineStep::new(line_term, 0, bytes.len());
1087:         while let Some((start, end)) = stepper.next(bytes) {
1088:             let line = Match::new(start, end);
1089:             self.write_prelude(
1090:                 self.sunk.absolute_byte_offset() + line.start() as u64,
1091:                 self.sunk.line_number().map(|n| n + count),
1092:                 Some(matches[0].start() as u64 + 1),
1093:             )?;
1094:             count += 1;
1095:             if self.exceeds_max_columns(&bytes[line]) {
1096:                 self.write_exceeded_line(bytes, line, matches, &mut midx)?;
1097:             } else {
1098:                 self.write_colored_matches(bytes, line, matches, &mut midx)?;
1099:                 self.write_line_term()?;
1100:             }
1101:         }
1102:         Ok(())
1103:     }
1104: 
1105:     fn sink_slow_multi_line_only_matching(&self) -> io::Result<()> {
1106:         let line_term = self.searcher.line_terminator().as_byte();
1107:         let spec = self.sink.replacer.color_matched();
1108:         let bytes = self.sunk.bytes();
1109:         let matches = self.sunk.matches();
1110:         let mut midx = 0;
1111:         let mut count = 0;
1112:         let mut stepper = LineStep::new(line_term, 0, bytes.len());
1113:         while let Some((start, end)) = stepper.next(bytes) {
1114:             let mut line = Match::new(start, end);
1115:             self.trim_line_terminator(bytes, &mut line);
1116:             self.trim_ascii_prefix(bytes, &mut line);
1117:             while !line.is_empty() {
1118:                 if matches[midx].end() <= line.start() {
1119:                     if midx + 1 < matches.len() {
1120:                         midx += 1;
1121:                         continue;
1122:                     } else {
1123:                         break;
1124:                     }
1125:                 }
1126:                 let m = matches[midx];
1127: 
1128:                 if line.start() < m.start() {
1129:                     let upto = cmp::min(line.end(), m.start());
1130:                     line = line.with_start(upto);
1131:                 } else {
1132:                     let upto = cmp::min(line.end(), m.end());
